name: test_mail_recovers_after_the_server_returns_even_under_traffic
description:
Once the server is back, mail should resume within a bound that does
not depend on the traffic falling silent.
descriptionHtml:
Once the server is back, mail should resume within a bound that does
not depend on the traffic falling silent.
statusMessage:
XFAIL VKJ-013: after the mail server restarts, the daemon keeps sending on the dead connection and only reconnects after a 30s idle gap, so steady traffic loses every message until it pauses

AssertionError: none of 5 messages sent over 25s of steady traffic arrived after the mail server came back; mail recovers only once traffic pauses
assert False
statusTrace:
anon = Actor(role='anon', auth=<vikunja_qa.auth.strategies.Anonymous object at 0x7fd496361480>, v1=<vikunja_qa.transport.clie...a_qa.transport.client.HttpClient object at 0x7fd495b9e210>, username='', email='', password='', user_id=None, extra={})
settings = Settings(base_url='http://localhost:3456', mailpit_url='http://localhost:18025', webhook_url='http://localhost:18080',..., attach_traffic=True, repository_url='https://github.com/petprojectsaqa/qa-framework-vikunja', contract_mode='strict')
mailpit = <vikunja_qa.transport.mailpit.MailpitClient object at 0x7fd4967ed7f0>

    @pytest.mark.finding("VKJ-013")
    @pytest.mark.xfail(
        reason=(
            "VKJ-013: after the mail server restarts, the daemon keeps sending on the dead "
            "connection and only reconnects after a 30s idle gap, so steady traffic loses every "
            "message until it pauses"
        ),
        # Not strict, for the same reason as the Redis one: this waits out a
        # thirty-second idle timer in the product and asks what happened within a
        # window, so a slow or a fast machine can change the answer without the
        # product having changed at all.
        strict=False,
    )
    def test_mail_recovers_after_the_server_returns_even_under_traffic(
        anon: Actor, settings: Settings, mailpit: MailpitClient
    ) -> None:
        """Once the server is back, mail should resume within a bound that does
        not depend on the traffic falling silent."""
        with stand.stopped("mailpit"):
            _request_a_mail(anon, settings)  # during the outage; poisons the connection
    
        sent = []
        deadline = time.monotonic() + _RECOVERY_WINDOW_S
        while time.monotonic() < deadline:
            sent.append(_request_a_mail(anon, settings))
            time.sleep(_STEADY_INTERVAL_S)
    
        delivered = any(mailpit.messages_for(email) for email in sent)
>       assert delivered, (
            f"none of {len(sent)} messages sent over {_RECOVERY_WINDOW_S}s of steady traffic arrived "
            "after the mail server came back; mail recovers only once traffic pauses"
        )
